sentences.text: His brother is a software engineer and he went to abroad i.e., America and was sending his saving/earnings to the petitioner's deceased husband instructing to purchase house site and plots at Nellore for development.
The deceased used to give the said amount by way of hand loan to the borrowers instead of purchasing house plots.
ii. On 25.12.2015 at about 9.30 p.m., the petitioner's husband consumed pesticide and became unconscious.
He was admitted in the hospital and while undergoing treatment, he was succumbed on 11.01.2016.
In respect of the same, a case in Crime No.6 of 2016 of I Town Police Station, Nellore has been registered under Section 174 Cr.P.C.

On 26.12.2016, the petitioner found two suicide notes,
one addressed to the SRK, J Superintendent of Police and the other is to his younger brother Mr.K.Srinivasa Reddy with his own hand writing and signatures.
Basing on the suicide report, the Section of law in the case in Crime No.6 of 2016 has been altered from Section 174 Cr.P.C. to Sections 306, 420 and 506 IPC.
After conducting investigation, the police filed charge sheet.

iii. Be that as it may, the un-official respondent i.e., 7th respondent had approached the Regional Passport Officer, Vijayawada and made an application through online by uploading the documents which are necessary to process the said application by concealing the fact that a case has been registered against him since 2016.
7th respondent obtained passport bearing No.X6746397, dated 20.03.2023 and fled away to abroad.

In connection with that, the petitioner herein made an application to respondent No.4 seeking documents that are uploaded by 7th respondent along with the copy of application so as to place the same before the Sessions Court to bring it to the notice of the Court.
Subsequently a representation has been made to 4th respondent herein to revoke the un-official respondent's passport.
Petitioner further submits that 7th respondent fled away to America on 11.07.2024.
4th respondent rejected the request of petitioner as if the information sought by her is under exemption under Section 8(1)(j) of RTI Act.

The petitioner further submits that she made a complaint before the United State Consular General, Gemeni Circle, Gopalapuram at Chennai, Tamilnadu 600 006 complaining that the un-official respondent availed visitors Visa K Sreevani vs Union Of India on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169718285/

sentences.text: SRK, J iv.
On 09.08.2024 and 14.09.2024, the petitioner made representations to 4th respondent.

In response to the representations made by the petitioner, 4th respondent passed an order on 14.10.2024 stating that 4th respondent has satisfied with the reply of CPIO, however, the petitioner has to submit certain certified copies in connection with the same, which are necessary for further action, if applicable as per extant norms.
In respect of the same, the petitioner though tried her level best to appear before the jurisdictional officer, her efforts have gone in vain.

3. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that though representations have been made, 4th respondent authorities have not given any opportunity of personal hearing and submitting the documents to 4th respondent.

4. On a bare perusal of the order dated 14.10.2024, 4th respondent has categorically observed to the extent that in any case any further documents are necessary for further action, if applicable as per extant norms, 4th respondent would look into the same.
5. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, this Court is of the view that an opportunity can be given to the petitioner herein to explain her case before 4th respondent authorities.

6. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is disposed of, with an observation that the petitioner herein is permitted to appear before the jurisdictional authority i.e., 4th respondent within a period of two (2)
weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order with all necessary documents and explain her case to the SRK, J respondent authorities.
Subsequently, the respondent authorities are directed to dispose of representations, if any, filed by petitioner herein in accordance with law within a period of four (4) weeks thereafter.
No order as to costs.
7. As a sequel thereto, the miscellaneous applications, if any, pending in this Writ Petition shall stand closed.

K. SREENIVASA REDDY, J.
